title: Ephemeral admission gate + hedged warmup and fast-fallback shim for burst-tolerant SLOs
author: Priya Desai
commits: introduce ephemeral admission gate and config schema
implement hedged warmup manager and KV priming path
integrate telemetry, tests, and k8s manifest updates
description:
Context: We saw a pattern of short-duration tenant bursts that caused clustered SLO violations because cold KV state and cold model caches delayed first responses and triggered downstream circuit breakers. Previous mitigations (longer prewarm windows and coarse throttles) either increased cost or introduced higher latency during steady state.

This PR introduces an 'Ephemeral Admission Gate' and a complementary 'Hedged Warmup' manager. The admission gate is a lightweight per-tenant connection/admission controller that applies a short, sliding priority window: new connections for low-priority tenants are admitted at a reduced rate while higher-priority tenants (or requests with active grace credits) can bypass. The Hedged Warmup manager creates a short-lived, speculative warmup path: when the gate delays a request, we kick off a low-cost hedged warmup that attempts to prime KV and token caches in parallel; if priming completes within the admission window, the request proceeds with warmed state. If priming fails or times out, the request falls back to a fast-degraded reply path (bounded short responses / partial content) rather than blocking and risking downstream cascades.

Goals: reduce spike-driven SLO violations, avoid long tail cold-start latency, keep incremental cost small during spikes, and provide operational knobs for tenants/regions.

What changed (single-string body): Implemented ephemeral admission gate (controlplane/admission/gate.go) with per-tenant sliding windows and crediting. Added HedgedWarmupManager (runtime/scheduler/warmup_manager.go) which schedules micro-warmups and coordinates with KV priming shim (runtime/kv/priming_shim.go). Exposed metrics for admission rates, warmup success latency histogram, and fallback-rate. Updated k8s manifest to deploy the admission controller as a sidecar optional for Dedicated and Private. Added integration smoke test to simulate burst patterns and verify SLOs under load (tests/integration/admission_smoke_test.py). Added metrics definitions and dashboards pointers in telemetry/metrics_definitions.yaml.

Checklist (what I validated): - Unit tests for admission gate logic (edge windows, credit decay) - Integration test that replays burst traces and asserts 99th p95 SLO improvement - Load lab run (synthetic tenant bursts) with telemetry snapshots attached - Lint, build, and e2e smoke passed in CI - Configuration defaults chosen to be conservative for existing deployments (feature gated off in release by default)

Operational details: - Default behavior: gate is feature-flagged off. When enabled, default sliding window = 3s, priority bucket sizes = [high, medium, low], initial grace credits = 10 per tenant/hour. - Hedged warmup TTLs: 150ms attempt window, KV priming uses lightweight HEAD request to internal cache service. - Fast-fallback behavior: when warmup fails, return a bounded partial reply with header 'X-Redwood-Degraded: true' and telemetry tag. This keeps invocations bounded and prevents long tail. - Admin surfaces: new route in console under 'SLO protections -> Admission Gate' (docs updated).

Backward compatibility & rollout: Gate is opt-in via feature flag. On Dedicated and Private customers we recommend staged rollouts per region with telemetry gating. No wire protocol changes.

Testing & evidence: - Load lab: 10K RPS burst for 30s across 200 tenants; with feature on p95 latency improved by 36% and p99 by 22% for high-priority tenants; fallback-rate stayed below 4%. - CI: unit + integration + smoke passed; metrics snapshot linked in Linear (ENG-2456).

Unresolved / future work: - Fine-tuning of grace-credit replenishment based on historical tenant patterns (follow-up ENG-2710). - More conservative KV priming strategies for low-memory nodes.

See commit summaries and changed files below for diffs. This PR is intended to be minimally invasive while providing a safe opt-in path for customers who want better spike resilience without giving up cost controls.

release_notes: Introduces an opt-in ephemeral admission gate and hedged warmup path to reduce spike-induced SLO violations. Feature gated by default; telemetry and runbook added.
